text:
Sophia: Quick follow-up on the RFC for release cohorts + pin migration. TL;DR: propose a lightweight 'cohort_fence' concept to express soft vs hard expiry, a migration grace window, and a compatibility fingerprint so runtime + clients can make safer decisions. Thoughts?

Liam: Can you paste a tiny schema sketch so we can react?

Sophia: Sure — crude sketch below (additive to model metadata):
```json
{
  "cohort_id": "2026-03-canary-01",
  "cohort_fence": "soft",        // soft | hard
  "expires_at": "2026-04-07T12:00:00Z",
  "grace_seconds": "86400",     // how long to accept mismatches after expiry
  "compatibility_sig": "sha256:9f...",
  "allowed_rollforward_seconds": "3600"  // client-side rollforward tolerance
}
```
This is intended to be runtime-forwarding friendly: soft fence = warn + telemetry + allow for grace_seconds; hard fence = block.

Raj: My concern: old clients that don't parse these fields might keep requesting incompatible pinned models. We should ensure runtime enforces hard fences regardless of client behavior. Soft fences also need a server-side opt-in for enforcement level (warn vs throttle).

Emilia: Related: how does this interact with prefix/KV caching and placement pins? If a cached KV was created under cohort A and then cohort A soft-expires, the cache entries should be annotated so we can evict or revalidate. Otherwise you'll get subtle correctness bugs.

Liam: Nice. How do we surface this in the public API? Response envelope + header? A new model-metadata endpoint?

Sophia: Proposed surface: 1) model metadata (already in catalog) gets these fields; 2) runtime returns an optional response header X-Model-Cohort: <id> and X-Model-Cohort-Status: soft|hard|expired for quick client heuristics; 3) a /v1/models/:id/metadata explainer for the console and dev tools. Backwards compatible because fields are additive.

Raj: For telemetry and rollbacks we should also emit events when a cohort transitions state (created -> soft_expired -> hard_expired) and include a correlate_id to tie to rollout jobs. Ops can alert on high client-side mismatch rates.

Emilia: +1 on cache annotation. Suggest we add cohort_id to KV cache keys and to the prefix cache entry metadata. Eviction policy: if cohort is hard_expired, evict; if soft_expired, mark stale and revalidate on read.

Liam: Edge case: what if a tenant pins a model to an old cohort intentionally? Do we allow tenant override? That seems dangerous if hard fence means incompatible binary. Need a tenant-level opt-in/override with strong audit trail.

Sophia: Agreed — propose tenant_override = {allowed: true|false, reason, author, expires_at}. Only allowed for soft fences; hard fences cannot be overridden. Audit logs + require admin role.

Raj: Implementation tactic: treat this as additive metadata. Runtime change: 1) parse cohort metadata at load; 2) enforce hard fences at request routing; 3) emit warnings for soft fences with grace_seconds; 4) expose metrics: cohort_mismatch_count, cohort_eviction_count, cohort_transition_events.

Emilia: Ops playbook snippet idea: when cohort_mismatch_count spikes, automatically pause cohort rollout and open a canary investigation. Could wire to existing rollout circuit breaker.

Sophia: Migration plan (high level):
- Phase 1: Add fields to catalog + console UI, no enforcement (emit warnings only).
- Phase 2: Runtime honors soft fences as warnings and optionally throttles mismatched tenants if config enabled.
- Phase 3: Runtime enforces hard fences; console shows action buttons to migrate or unpin.

Liam: Sounds reasonable. Who wants to own the follow-up RFC? I'll volunteer to draft the enforcement matrix if Sophia fills in the schema details and Emilia drafts cache changes.

Sophia: I'll draft schema and the example use-cases. Emilia — can you take cache change doc? Liam — enforcement matrix. Raj — telemetry/metrics events. I'll circulate a short RFC next week. :+1: :eyes:

deploy-bot: Staging job started for "cohort-fence-prototype" (#342) — build 88 deployed to staging. Logs: https://staging.internal/release/342/logs

Raj: Thanks. One more nit: name suggestion: use "cohort_fence" not "fence_type" to avoid colliding with other fencing concepts.

Emilia: LGTM. I'll stub the KV annotation PR after Sophia's schema lands.

Sophia: Great — next step: RFC draft + minimal JSON schema + simple console mock. Will ping when ready.

Liam: +1, thanks everyone.
